summary: Verified 2026 signals materially strengthen the case for an edge-first, simulation-heavy AETHERHOME stack with human fallback: Google DeepMind has moved Gemini Robotics 2 and an on-device VLA into whole-body and local robot control; NVIDIA now offers an open GR00T humanoid reference stack around Jetson Thor; Figure reports >350 Figure 03 units produced and a ramp from one robot/day to one/hour; U.S. AV policy is becoming more deployment-friendly. These are industry signals, not evidence that AETHERHOME itself is technically ready, funded, partnered or deployed.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: Gemini Robotics 2 adds whole-body VLA control and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 is designed for local general-purpose manipulation; NVIDIA's GR00T reference design combines an open humanoid stack with Jetson Thor.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: ATLAS should be architected around swappable local VLA/embodied-reasoning policies, explicit safety constraints and teleoperation fallback rather than assuming one proprietary end-to-end model will solve every task.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: Figure says its new Index data pipeline has processed 16M+ human-task videos from 100+ countries, while current VLA systems increasingly combine human video, robot demonstrations, simulation and synthetic trajectories.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: AETHERHOME's durable moat is more likely to come from cabin-specific task data, evaluation and recovery policies than from training a frontier foundation model from scratch.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: NVIDIA Jetson Thor is generally available with up to 2,070 FP4 TFLOPS, 128 GB memory and 40-130 W power; NVIDIA Marketplace lists the AGX Thor developer kit at $5,499, but availability and regional pricing vary.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: A full local perception/reasoning tier is plausible for prototype work, but this price is a public developer-kit price, not a production BOM quote.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: Lambda currently lists single-GPU H100 PCIe at $3.29/GPU-hour, H100 SXM at $4.29/GPU-hour and B200 at $6.99/GPU-hour; AWS Capacity Blocks list H100 P5.4xlarge around $4.72/GPU-hour in Mumbai and $5.191 in several U.S. regions.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: bursty cloud training/simulation remains preferable to owning frontier training infrastructure at AETHERHOME's current stage; production inference should be pushed to edge hardware wherever latency and safety require it.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: NVIDIA says BYD, Geely, Isuzu and Nissan are adopting DRIVE Hyperion for Level-4-ready vehicles, while NHTSA announced first-ever AV performance standards work and a temporary exemption allowing Zoox up to 2,500 commercial vehicles annually for two years.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: AETHERHOME should integrate with a certified autonomy/vehicle platform instead of building a road-driving stack from first principles; P4 remains correctly separated from cabin robotics.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: Figure reports >350 Figure 03 robots delivered from BotQ and a production-rate increase from one/day to one/hour; Agility opened a 60,000-sq-ft Physical AI facility complementing its RoboFab manufacturing operation.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: humanoid development is entering fleet-learning and manufacturing phases, but vendor-reported throughput does not prove broad reliability, unit economics or suitability for a moving-home environment.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: ISO 10218-1:2025 and 10218-2:2025 define updated industrial robot and robot-cell safety requirements; the EU AI Act became broadly applicable on 2 August 2026, while U.S. AV exemptions are being streamlined.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: safety cases, logging, fail-safe behavior, human override and regulatory traceability should be first-class software architecture concerns now, not deferred certification work.

signals.headline: VERIFIED SIGNAL: current public Bay Area robotics postings show roughly $150K-$250K base for lead robotics-platform roles and about $180K-$250K for senior embedded humanoid roles, usually plus equity; individual offers vary.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: U.S. senior robotics integration talent remains expensive, reinforcing a small senior core plus global engineering/contractor model for early phases.

signals.headline: VERIFIED: Apptronik says its Series A reached >$935M; Figure previously announced >$1B Series C at a $39B post-money valuation; Xpeng Robotics announced >$900M in its first external round at >$6.3B valuation.
signals.impact: INFERENCE: frontier humanoid hardware is exceptionally capital-intensive. AETHERHOME should continue financing by capability milestones instead of positioning a concept-stage company as comparable in readiness or valuation.

cost_watch.gpu: Public 2026 spot/on-demand pricing remains highly variable. Current official reference points: Lambda 1x H100 PCIe $3.29/hr, H100 SXM $4.29/hr, B200 $6.99/hr; AWS H100 Capacity Blocks about $4.72/hr in Mumbai and $5.191/hr in several U.S. regions. Treat as transient public pricing, not contracted quotes.
cost_watch.talent: Public U.S. robotics postings continue to indicate roughly $150K-$250K+ base for senior/lead robotics-platform and embedded roles, often plus equity. Treat as directional hiring-market evidence, not a compensation budget quote.
cost_watch.prototype: No verified evidence this week justifies changing the existing journey cost bands. Jetson Thor's public $5,499 developer-kit price is useful for edge-compute prototyping but is not a production BOM.

roadmap_updates: No phase or cost-band change this week. Strengthen P1/P3 around edge-first VLA evaluation, teleoperation fallback, task-data capture and safety logging; retain P4 as integration with a certified vehicle/autonomy platform rather than first-principles road autonomy.
